title: Has China Obtained the World's Most Important Machine?

vocab.articleQuote: …it will probably not be the last time that ASML and its coveted technology are caught in the crossfire.
vocab.inContext: It describes ASML's machine-making technology as something governments and companies around the world desperately want to get their hands on.
vocab.meaning: Coveted means eagerly wanted and prized by many people — so desirable that others envy whoever has it.
examples: A starting spot on the varsity team is coveted by every freshman who tries out.
The corner desk by the window was the most coveted seat in the whole classroom.

vocab.articleQuote: But this is just an early salvo in the bigger battle over AI chokeholds.
vocab.inContext: The fight over the alleged machine is called just the opening shot in a much longer struggle between the US and China over control of AI technology.
vocab.meaning: A salvo is a sudden burst — originally of several guns firing at once — now often used for an opening or aggressive move in a larger conflict or argument.
examples: Her sharp first question was the opening salvo in a debate that ran for an hour.
The store's surprise price cut was a salvo aimed straight at its biggest rival.

vocab.articleQuote: …it knows the exact location of all 340 EUV machines it has produced, including 26 decommissioned ones.
vocab.inContext: The 26 machines that have been retired and taken out of active use — but whose whereabouts ASML says it still tracks.
vocab.meaning: To decommission something is to officially take it out of active service, especially a machine, ship, power plant, or weapon.
examples: The old aircraft carrier was decommissioned and turned into a floating museum.
When the new lab opened, the school decommissioned its twenty-year-old computers.

vocab.articleQuote: The fracas over Mr Lutnick's claim may die down, especially if America fails to share supporting evidence.
vocab.inContext: The noisy public dispute and uproar set off by the US commerce secretary's accusation about the machine.
vocab.meaning: A fracas is a noisy quarrel, uproar, or disorderly commotion, usually involving several people.
examples: A fracas broke out in the stands after the referee's controversial call.
The group chat erupted into a fracas over who was really to blame for the lost match.

concepts.name: The semiconductor supply chain
concepts.articleQuote: These machines, whose creations power the most capable artificial-intelligence models, are made only by ASML, a Dutch company.
concepts.inContext: In the article, the world's best AI chips can only be manufactured using EUV machines, and those machines are built by exactly one company — the Dutch firm ASML. That is why a single Dutch machine sits at the center of a US–China superpower fight.
concepts.meaning: Making an advanced computer chip is a relay race split across a few hyper-specialized companies, and almost none of them does more than one leg. First, a designer like Nvidia decides what the chip should do — but Nvidia owns no factories; it is 'fabless.' Next, a foundry actually manufactures the chip, 'printing' billions of microscopic transistors onto silicon wafers; in the real world the dominant foundry is Taiwan's TSMC (the article doesn't name it, but that's who makes chips like Nvidia's). To carve features only a few atoms wide, the foundry needs lithography machines, and the most advanced kind — extreme-ultraviolet, or EUV — is built by just one company on Earth: ASML in the Netherlands (older, less precise DUV machines are far more widely available). So the path behind a single AI chip runs Nvidia (design) → a foundry like TSMC (fabrication) → ASML (the machine that makes fabrication possible) — three near-monopolies in three different countries, each holding a piece no rival can easily replace. That is why 'just build your own' is so hard, and why controlling any one link is so powerful.

concepts.name: Export controls
concepts.articleQuote: Since 2019 America has blocked the export to China of the extreme ultraviolet, or EUV, lithography machines that make the world's most advanced semiconductors.
concepts.inContext: The US has legally banned the sale of the most advanced chip-making machines to China, aiming to slow China's progress in AI and advanced computing.
concepts.meaning: Export controls are government rules that restrict or forbid selling certain goods, technologies, or know-how to particular countries — usually for national-security reasons. They differ from a tariff, which merely taxes a sale: an export control can block the sale outright. Governments reach for them to deny a rival access to strategic technology — advanced chips, weapons parts, encryption — betting that if you control something the other side can't easily make for itself, withholding it slows them down. Their reach can even stretch beyond a country's own borders when the restricted item depends on that country's technology, which is how the US can pressure a Dutch company's sales to China.

quiz.question: What is the core dispute the article describes?
options: China has publicly admitted buying an ASML machine
The US alleges an EUV machine may have reached China, while ASML insists it tracks all 340 it ever made and none is there
ASML has announced it is moving its headquarters to China
The US and the Netherlands have agreed to start selling EUV machines to China
quiz.explanation: The piece centers on a US allegation that an EUV machine may have reached China, which ASML flatly denies, saying it knows the location of all 340 machines it has ever produced.

quiz.question: In the chip supply chain, what does a 'fabless' company like Nvidia actually do?
options: It builds the lithography machines used to make chips
It manufactures its chips in its own factories
It designs chips but relies on other companies to manufacture them
It mines the raw silicon that chips are made from
quiz.explanation: 'Fabless' means a company designs chips but owns no fabrication plants, so a foundry (such as TSMC) does the actual manufacturing.

quiz.question: Why has the US used export controls to block sales of EUV machines to China?
options: To collect more tax revenue from Chinese imports
To lower the price of chips for American buyers
To deny China a strategic technology it can't easily build itself, slowing its AI progress
To force ASML to move its factories to the United States
quiz.explanation: Export controls ban selling strategic technology to a rival; the US bet that withholding EUV machines China cannot yet make itself would slow its advance in AI.

quiz.question: In the sentence "ASML and its coveted technology," the word coveted most nearly means:
options: outdated and unwanted
eagerly desired by many
kept completely secret
cheap and easy to copy
quiz.explanation: Coveted describes something many people strongly want and even envy — here, technology everyone would love to control.

quiz.question: The article calls the current clash "just an early salvo in the bigger battle." A salvo is:
options: a peaceful compromise
a final surrender
an opening or aggressive move in a conflict
a small, harmless accident
quiz.explanation: A salvo is a burst (originally of gunfire) used figuratively to mean an opening or aggressive move in a larger fight.
